chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I recited: 'Al-Ta'iboon Al-Abidoun' (The Repentant, the Worshippers). He said: 'Do not recite Al-Ta'ibeen Al-Abideen up to its end.' I was asked about the reason for that, and he said: 'He bought from the believers, the repentant, the worshippers.'
ai.seo_question: Why should 'Al-Ta'iboon Al-Abidoun' in Surah At-Tawbah not be read as a single compound phrase?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) elucidates that the grammatical structure of 'Al-Ta'iboon Al-Abidoun' in Surah At-Tawbah 9:112 is syntactically linked to the subsequent phrase 'Ashra min al-Mu'minina,' indicating that God purchased the believers who are characterized by repentance and worship. This reading preserves the theological integrity of the verse by affirming that the believers themselves are the object of divine purchase, rather than treating 'repentant' and 'worshipping' as an isolated compound entity. This nuance highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise recitation (Qira'at) reflecting deeper theological realities regarding the status of the faithful.
